notes.title: Bank Korean
notes.text: Take a number (번호표) and wait to be called. Handy phrases: 통장을 만들고 싶어요 (I'd like to open an account), 돈을 찾고 싶어요 (I'd like to withdraw money), 돈을 보내고 싶어요 (I'd like to send money). Staff use honorific nouns for customers — 성함 (name), 연세 (age) — and -아/어 주시겠어요? for requests.

notes.title: 용돈
notes.text: 용돈 is pocket money — for kids from their parents and, in a lovely reversal, for parents from their grown-up children, especially on holidays and birthdays. Errands are 심부름; running one for an elder is a classic way for a kid to earn a little 용돈.

notes.title: -(으)ㄹ 테니까
notes.text: -(으)ㄹ 테니까 = "since (I) will…, (you) do…": 제가 청소할 테니까 요리해 주세요 (I'll clean, so you cook). It's how Koreans split up chores and plans. Post office words: 소포를 부치다 (send a package), 택배 (courier delivery), 포장 (packing — and also "to go" at restaurants: 포장해 주세요).

lessons.goal: Use passive verbs: 열리다, 들리다, 보이다.

notes.title: Passive verbs
notes.text: Some verbs have a passive twin made with 이, 히, 리 or 기: 보다 → 보이다 (be seen), 듣다 → 들리다 (be heard), 열다 → 열리다 (open by itself), 닫다 → 닫히다 (shut by itself). 문을 열었어요 = I opened the door; 문이 열렸어요 = the door opened. Letters to elders begin with …께 (honorific "to").

lessons.goal: Talk about visiting and meeting people.

notes.title: Visiting words
notes.text: 찾아가다 = go to see someone, 찾아오다 = come to see, 들르다 = drop by on the way, 다녀가다 = come by briefly, 마중 나가다 = go out to meet someone arriving, 배웅하다 = see someone off. 방문 means both "visit" (訪問) and "room door" (房門) — context tells you which.

lessons.goal: Say where things are: 맞은편, 건너편.

notes.title: Location words
notes.text: 맞은편 = directly opposite, 건너편 = across (a street or river), 곳곳 / 여기저기 / 이곳저곳 = here and there, everywhere. An 오피스텔 is a studio-style office-residence, popular with young singles. Big apartment estates are 아파트 단지.
